newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods flat in directionless market.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods flat in directionless market.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices were flat Monday, with little direction from local spot markets or futures trade, brokers said.
On NYMEX, unleaded gasoline for July delivery rose a mere 0.18 cents a gallon to 62.99 cents, while the nearby heating oil contract edged up 0.48 cents a gallon to 56.32 cents.
"The (New York Mercantile Exchange) was flat and there's nothing new in our market, so nothing moved," one California broker said.
ARCO confirmed its 43,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker at the Carson refinery near Los Angeles returned to service last Friday and caused flaring.
The distillate-making unit was shut for maintenance May 2.
Regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline was pegged between 62.50 and 63.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, flat from Friday.
Regular conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was pegged at between 59 and 60 cents a gallon, also steady.

++ DISTILLATE prices in Los Angeles were steady, with CARB-grade low sulphur, low aromatic diesel pegged at 64/65 cents a gallon. But traders said the return of ARCO's hydrocracker could weaken distillate prices slightly.
EPA-grade diesel was steady in Los Angeles at 59/60 cents Monday.
Two cargoes of EPA were scheduled to leave the San Francisco area for Asia this week, traders said.
